answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a trellis as the anchor of the cost.
